issues.claim: CCTV produced a crime reduction of 'about 13% versus control areas' (measured_outcomes, strength High)
issues.problem: The cited URL (OJP abstract page) describes a 'significant and modest decrease' but does not display the 13% figure. The number is correct, but it is not on the page the brief cites.
issues.fix: Cite the study text that carries the figure (same authors' Brå/Cambridge report, pooled OR 1.141 = ~13% reduction) or the Wiley DOI 10.1111/1745-9133.12419, in addition to the OJP abstract.

issues.claim: NRF subsequently stopped publishing an industry-wide shrink rate because retailers calculate it differently
issues.problem: Stated as fact without a source in the entry, which cites only the 2023 NRF press release. The underlying fact is corroborated elsewhere (Retail Dive, Oct 2024; NRF blog) but is not sourced in the brief.
issues.fix: Add a citation for the discontinuation, or label the sentence as reported/unverified.

issues.problem: Every figure used was read from the arXiv v1 preprint; the entry itself states the journal version returned HTTP 403 and was not readable. Labelling the study type 'peer-reviewed' is inconsistent with the sourcing described, even though strength is correctly Low.

issues.claim: Problem summary: 2C:14-9 'makes it a third-degree crime to record another person's intimate parts, or fourth-degree for undergarment-clad intimate parts, where a reasonable person would not expect to be observed'
issues.problem: Statute also requires the recording be 'without that person's consent'; the summary omits that element. Not a misstatement of the offense, but an incomplete statement of a criminal rule in the headline paragraph.
issues.fix: Add 'without consent' to the one-line summary so it matches 2C:14-9(b).

issues.problem: No vendor outcome claims are rated above Low (correct). Two judgement calls sit at the generous end: the NRF shrink figure is Medium although it is a self-selected online survey of senior LP executives (the entry itself notes it is not a probability sample), and the CCTV meta-analysis is High although it is a public-space literature base, not small-retail evidence.
issues.fix: Optional: add a one-line note that the CCTV evidence base is public-space studies, so transfer to a 5-100 staff shop is an inference.
